title: Finite Gram perturbation bridge for OS context changes
question: Can an exact finite Gram-entry perturbation inequality translate OS context changes into explicit vector-difference terms, while keeping the actual Q3 common-Hilbert-space and uniformity hypotheses open?

exact_statement.gram_entry: G_f(i,j)=sum_k f(i,k) f(j,k) for finite real vectors.
exact_statement.interpretation: The first term controls change in the left OS word and the second controls change in the right OS word; both vector families and the finite index set remain explicit.

adversarial_review.check: The inequality is stated for a finite coordinate index with an explicit Fintype and DecidableEq hypothesis; no infinite-volume sum is hidden.
The identity f_i f_j-g_i g_j=(f_i-g_i)f_j+g_i(f_j-g_j) is proved by ring and the absolute-value triangle inequality is applied before summation.
R339 is deliberately Real-valued; it is not asserted to be a Complex physical-sector positivity or QFT state theorem.
The two terms are only finite coordinate-vector differences; identifying them with actual Q3 OS transfer-word differences requires a separate common-carrier and normalization proof.
The integer fixture is a self-test oracle for the general inequality and is not used as a physical Q3 value or asymptotic estimate.
Primary and independent lanes reconstruct the exact sums separately, while the integrated lane reruns both and the pinned Lean theorem.
No source, volume, cutoff or beta uniform constant is inferred from one finite fixture.
The bridge does not close a common OS carrier, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, common alpha, GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A.

lean_crosscheck.role: R339 is the exact finite algebraic bridge from Gram-entry changes to two vector-difference sums. It leaves the actual Q3 OS vector factorization and all uniform estimates as explicit hypotheses.

qft_interface.closed: For finite real vector families, a Gram entry difference is bounded by the sum of the left-word and right-word vector differences weighted by the companion vectors.
qft_interface.open: Actual Q3 transfer-word vector representations, common OS Hilbert carrier, source/volume/cutoff/beta-uniform vector bounds, exhaustion Cauchy, direct D/delta-D convergence, common alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary finite QFT bridge only; no physical reference, heat-root incidence, canonical A1/R-192 production owner, Sector-A closure or Pre-A closure is supplied.

next_action: Instantiate the two vector-difference terms on the committed finite Q3 OS transfer-word data, with explicit normalization and source/volume/cutoff/beta controls. If no common vector factorization can be certified, record that obstruction rather than treating Gram decay as vector Cauchy convergence.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite Gram perturbation theorem and exact fixture. It is not an analytic uniformity theorem, a thermodynamic OS construction, a mass-gap proof, a continuum result, or a Clay result.
no_overclaim: This package proves only the declared finite Real Gram-entry inequality and its exact fixture reproduction. It does not prove actual Q3 OS vector convergence, a common Hilbert carrier, common alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, a GNS mass gap, continuum removal, C6, Sector A, Pre-A or a Clay result.
